plan.title: Welcome text reads like a form

transcript.text:
Hey, I'm ZOH! I'll help you get better at one thing with a small step each day. Text "stop" anytime, and tell me anytime how you want coaching ("chill out", "push me harder").

What's your name, and what are you looking to work on?

• Put AI to work for you
• Read & learn more (books, ideas, any topic)
• Start something on the side
• Focus & get more done
• Speak & connect better
• Get fitter
• Eat better
• Sleep better
• Learn a fun skill (Rubik's cube, card trick, play a song, drawing)
• Not sure? Let's figure it out together
Alex. Exercise, wanna get back to the gym
Let's go, Alex. What did you usually do back when you were going to the gym?

checks.reason: Plain text and a • list with no markdown, hashtags or filler.
Warm, direct opener with "Hey, I'm ZOH!" and no emoji row.
Asks only for name and goal, using the ten-starter list.
Nothing already given is asked for.
Makes no claims beyond what the product does.
Asks no wake, sleep, pushiness or city question.
Two short sentences with one question.
Plain conversational text with no markdown or filler.
"Let's go, Alex." is warm and energetic without overfamiliarity.
Asks what they used to do at the gym, which fits getting back to it.
Does not re-ask for the name or goal Alex already gave.
Uses only what Alex said about the gym.
Stays on the goal of getting back to the gym.
No wake, sleep, pushiness or city question.

conversation.reason: First text now gives intro, stop and style lines, asks only name and goal, and lists the ten starters ending with "Not sure?"; the next question fits the gym goal and is a single question.

grade.summary: ZOH fixed the regression: its first text now introduces itself, explains stop and coaching changes, asks only for name and goal, and shows the starter list in one message. Its reply to Alex stays on the gym goal with one fitting question and no numbered questionnaire.
